Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

C0036 · Circumcise the covenant males in the foreskin, including household-born and purchased males, with newborns circumcised on the eighth day

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

17:10 This is the covenant that you shall keep between Me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations: every male among you shall be circumcised.

17:11 You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

17:12 At eight days old every male child among you shall be circumcised throughout your generations, whether born in your household or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.

17:13 Both the one born in your household and the one bought with money must surely be circumcised. My covenant shall be upon your flesh as an everlasting covenant.

17:14 An uncircumcised male whose foreskin flesh is not circumcised on the eighth day—that person shall be destroyed from his kin; he has scattered My covenant.”

Genesis 17:10–14

21:4 Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day, as God had commanded him.

Genesis 21:4

12:44 And every man’s household slave, or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise; and then he shall eat of it.

Exodus 12:44

12:48 But if a resident foreigner comes to you to keep the Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male belonging to him; and then he shall draw near to keep it, and shall be as the native of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it.

Exodus 12:48

12:3 And on the eighth day he shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.

Leviticus 12:3

Audience: A shared rule for the people, office or circumstances specified in the source. Preserve its covenant, priestly, civil or ritual limits and the existing fulfillment classification.

Classification: Transformed · Torah requirement

Topic: Covenant signs, vows and dedications

Physical circumcision is not made a condition of Gentile salvation. Paul speaks of circumcision in Christ and directs people called while uncircumcised not to seek circumcision as a covenant requirement.

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

17:10 This is the covenant that you shall keep between Me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations: every male among you shall be circumcised.

17:11 You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

17:13 Both the one born in your household and the one bought with money must surely be circumcised. My covenant shall be upon your flesh as an everlasting covenant.

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Covenant signs, vows and dedications

Connection to Christ: Acts and Galatians explicitly reject requiring circumcision for Gentile salvation.
